gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahlav: Tightly packed retro lettering with a bossy, crowded look up top. Styro huddles its letters together while Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi lets its e gape wide, so the page moves from squeeze to release.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Chunky retro letters jammed shoulder to shoulder, set the tone. Across a full page of text, Noto Sans Samaritan lets daylight into every curve, so the reading loosens up after the cramped Styro heading.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Noto Sans Sundanese leaves its e crossbars open, and its caps barely rise above the lowercase. And Styro crowds retro letters into a commanding block, which is what it does best, while the body simply stays readable.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Retro and commanding, with letters pushed hard against each other. Styro does that squeezed, loud display job best, while Noto Sans Sunuwar uses curves with real daylight in them to keep its sans text approachable.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Styro packs retro, commanding letters tightly, leaving hardly any gap inside its curves. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri brings short ascenders and a tall x-height, so its sans-serif text reads smoothly down a full page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern reads friendly and current, its curve endings keeping well away from one another. Styro shouts in retro tones up top, and the sans-serif text beneath keeps going line after line without strain.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Noto Sans Tagalog is a sans-serif whose lowercase dominates the line, with generous gaps left in its curves. Noto Sans Tagalog then loosens up the page under the retro, crowded Styro heading.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Retro letters squeezed together, all command and very little gap. Noto Sans Tagbanwa sits beneath Styro and fills most of the line height with open curves, which lets the crowded heading breathe out.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads softly, its sans-serif strokes tapering out before they touch and its capitals barely rising above the lowercase. Beneath the crowded Styro heading, longer text keeps flowing without a snag.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified without changing size, its terminals stopping far from the stem. Noto Sans Tamil is best at open, modern text, while Styro does its finest work as a tight, retro, commanding heading.
